title: Regional residency: technical tactics & rollforward plan (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Working draft of the technical tactics we will use to implement tenant/region pinning at scale across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Focused on: deterministic routing (pin table), enforcement bridges (edge proxies & connectors), operator rollforward plan, telemetry gating and reconciliation/eviction strategies.
- This is NOT the legal policy doc — include the legal checklist we need to validate per-customer after engineering changes land.

High-level approach summary (TL;DR):
1) Maintain a canonical Pin Store (pin-service) that holds tenant->region mapping and binding metadata (pin reason, TTL, source: customer/contract/admin).
2) Enforce pins at the routing layer (region-aware proxy) with two modes: strict (hard-enforce, fail fast) and best-effort (soft-mark + telemetry) for gradual rollout.
3) Ship a reconciliation/eviction worker that detects drift and auto-suggests remediation cases to operators (with human-in-loop for high-risk customers).
4) Gate release with telemetry SLOs and unit tests that exercise cross-region fallback, evidence packaging, and audit logs.

Key design decisions (decided / proposed):
- Canonical store format: JSON records keyed by tenant_id with fields: pinned_region, pin_source, effective_at, expires_at (nullable), enforcement_mode (strict|soft|disabled), audit_refs (list).
- Pin resolution precedence: explicit customer pin > contract-mandated pin > service-default-region.
- Fallback policy: when strict enforcement fails due to capacity/zone outage, automatically degrade to nearest eligible region (based on affinity scores and legal compatibility) and mark an exception-event with evidence package.
- Enforcement agent placement: region-aware proxies in edge zones (closest to customer region) that fetch pin metadata from local cache + periodic TTL refresh from pin-service.

Operator rollforward plan (one-page runbook):
- Phase 0 (canary): soft-mode only. Enable soft enforcement for 10 pilot tenants (low traffic, varied geos) — goal: surface telemetry signals and false positives. Owners: Priya (infra), Noah (runtime). JIRA: PRIV-621.
- Phase 1 (limited strict): move a small cohort (20–30 tenants) to strict enforcement during low-traffic windows. Operators will monitor error rates and latency delta. Owners: Maya (eng lead), Ethan (sre). JIRA: PRIV-664.
- Phase 2 (business-critical): expand strict mode to high-volume enterprise tenants with contractual pins, runbook confirmed with Legal & CS. If rollback needed, use automated rollback toggle per-tenant. JIRA: PRIV-709.

Acceptance criteria and gating telemetry (what to watch before next phase):
- Pin resolution success rate >= 99.95% (synthetic + production sampling). Metric: pin_resolve.success_ratio (tagged by region, deployment-type).
- Edge cache hit ratio >= 98% to avoid spiky load on pin-service. Metric: pin_cache.hit_rate.
- No increase > 2x in 5xxs attributable to pin enforcement path for canary tenants over baseline window. Metric: http.5xx.rate with blame tag.
- SLA regressions: p50/p95 latency for generation requests not degrade by >10% during enforcement window.
- Audit evidence completeness: >99% of pinned requests must have an audit_ref attached in logs.

Reconciliation and eviction worker (detailed notes):
- Purpose: ensure actual routing & storage residency matches pin metadata. Reconcile every 4 hours for strict tenants, 24 hours for soft.
- Heuristics: mismatch if (request_region != pinned_region) OR (storage_location != pinned_region) for >= 5 sampled events in 12h window.
- Eviction flow: mark tenant for operator review, attach sample request traces and storage objects; propose candidate remediation (re-pin, migrate storage, or escalate to contract team).
- Auto-eviction: only for temporary pins with short TTLs and low-risk customers; requires two independent checks and admin approval.

Operator tooling & quick commands (to include in ops kit):
- Inspect pin for tenant: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://pin-service.internal/v1/tenants/<tenant>/pin
- Force re-fetch on proxy: POST /_admin/pin-cache/invalidate?tenant=<tenant>
- Toggle enforcement mode: PATCH /v1/tenants/<tenant>/pin {"enforcement_mode":"soft"} (audit logged)
- Reconciliation dry-run: /internal/reconcile?tenant=<tenant>&dry_run=true -> returns suggested actions JSON

QA and automated tests matrix (must be added to CI):
- Unit tests for pin resolution precedence, TTL expiry behavior, and enforcement_mode toggles.
- Integration tests: simulate proxy cache misses, pin-service latency > 200ms fallbacks, and verify fallback evidence packaging.
- E2E (staging): cross-region traffic simulation with storage anchor verification (S3 bucket region tags), contracts flagged scenario.

Open risk matrix (notes / TODOs):
- Risk: legal/regulatory nuance mismatch between region boundaries (e.g., EU vs. EFTA). TODO: bring in Legal to enumerate territory boundaries per contract. Owner: Sofia. JIRA: PRIV-734.
- Risk: capacity constraints when strict enforcement sends traffic to a single pinned region. Mitigation: capacity reservations (Dedicated) + burst fallback. Short-term: add quota buffer per-tenant. Owner: Ethan.
- Risk: audit data growth and retention cost. Mitigation: compress audit refs and offload older evidence to cold storage with indexed summary. Owner: Maya.

Communication & customer-facing plan (ops + CS):
- Pre-change notice: automated email to pinned customers 72h before strict enforcement change (includes expected impact & rollback contact). Template in CS drive.
- Runbook for incidents: standardized incident template that includes evidence package and suggested messaging (customer-specific).
- Post-change debrief: 24–48h post-phase summary: pin_resolve metrics, false-positive incidents, latency impact, and customer feedback.

Migration & storage considerations (sticky notes):
- For customers that require data anchor migration: plan migration windows, cost estimate, S3 replication considerations, and deletion strategy of prior-region copies. We must avoid dual-write during migration unless contract allows.
- Consider using temporary region escrow for contract transitions where allowed.

Unresolved questions (explicit):
- Should pin TTLs default to infinite unless contract specifies? Pros: stable routing; cons: stale pins after org-level changes. Proposal: default infinite but require periodic owner confirmation for enterprise accounts.
- How to represent multi-region pins (EU-1 primary, EU-2 backup) in pin model? Need a small schema extension: prioritised_region_list.
- Exact evidence package schema — what artifacts must it include for legal audit: request traces, proxy headers, geo-ip evidence, dataset identifiers. Attach sample schema to this doc when approved.

Sprint backlog (short actionable items with owners):
- PRIV-821: Implement pin-service record schema migration to add enforcement_mode and audit_refs (owner: Noah)
- PRIV-822: Proxy cache invalidation endpoint and TLS cert rotation tests (owner: Priya)
- PRIV-823: Reconciliation worker scaffolding + sample UI for operator suggested actions (owner: Ethan)
- PRIV-824: Telemetry dashboards (pin_resolve.* metrics, cache hit, enforcement-induced 5xxs) (owner: Sofia)
- PRIV-825: Email templates and CS runbook (owner: Maya, collaborator: CS team)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep canary group heterogeneous: mix of Hosted/Dedicated/Private and multi-tenancy shapes.
- Coordinate with release-engineering for feature flag gating (we want kill-switch per-tenant + global).
- Add metric correlation: tag enforcement events with pin_source so we can filter legal vs user pins.

Appendix: quick sample pin record (example only):
- tenant_id: "acme-corp"
- pinned_region: "eu-west-1"
- enforcement_mode: "strict"
- pin_source: "contract:EU-data-boundary-2024"
- effective_at: "2024-11-01T00:00:00Z"
- audit_refs: ["evidence-20250201-423"]

Next steps / meeting asks:
- Sync with Legal on evidence schema (Sofia to lead) — target: 2025-03-05
- Demo canary to leadership with telemetry snapshot — target: before Phase 1 sign-off
- Add QA tickets to PRIV epic and schedule the e2e window.

If you read this and have immediate objections to the fallback policy (auto-degrade to nearest compatible region) flag in Slack #priv-deployments — that fallback is conservative but will need legal sign-off for some customers.

----
Document history: notes & quick edits:
- 2024-11-07: initial brainstorming (Maya)
- 2024-12-02: added reconciliation heuristics (Noah)
- 2025-01-14: operator rollforward plan fleshed out (Priya & Ethan)
- 2025-02-28: added sprint backlog and QA matrix (Maya)
plain_text_summary: Draft technical tactics and operator rollforward plan for implementing region pinning and residency enforcement. Includes runbook phases, reconciliation worker design, telemetry gates, operator commands, sprint backlog and unresolved legal/operational questions.
